speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Brisket nods slowly. "Go on in. Mind the cheese."
after: Brisket nods slowly, at a point somewhere above your head. "You may go in. One does ask that you mind the cheese."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "The cheese takes trespassing personally. You're walking on its rind."
after: "The cheese takes trespassing rather personally, you see, since it is its rind you are walking on."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Brisket sniffs the air, and his eyes close in bliss. "Saffron. Real saffron."
after: Brisket sniffs the air, and his eyes close in bliss. "Saffron. That is real saffron, and I had begun to think I should never smell it again."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "Do you know how long it has been?" He takes the threads with great tenderness and steps aside.
after: "Do you have any idea how long it has been?" He takes the threads with great tenderness and steps aside.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "Go on through. Tell the Cheddar Cliffs they are overdue for a good grating. Yes, Chef."
after: "Go on through, and kindly tell the Cheddar Cliffs they are overdue for a good grating. Yes, Chef."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Brisket does not look at you. He looks over your head, at the horizon. "This gate opens for one pinch of saffron."
after: Brisket does not look at you. He looks over your head, at the horizon. "This gate opens for one pinch of saffron, and I regret to say that it opens for nothing else."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "Real saffron, mind you, which grows in the Candy Field. Ask a sous-chef if you lose your way."
after: "Real saffron, mind you, which grows in the Candy Field. Should you lose your way, you may ask a sous-chef."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: He sighs at you. "Bring saffron from the Candy Field; this gate has a very particular taste in visitors."
after: He sighs at you. "Bring saffron from the Candy Field, if you would. This gate has a very particular taste in visitors, and so, I am afraid, have I."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Sir Loin raises his fork in salute. "You mended Old Meatloaf, so you are a friend of the Pantry. The town is yours."
after: Sir Loin raises his fork in salute. "Well met! You mended Old Meatloaf, and so you are a friend of the Pantry, and the town is yours for as long as I keep this gate."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Sir Loin inspects you. "Old Meatloaf walks again. Basil sends thanks, and orders, which are: let you in. Yes, Chef!"
after: Sir Loin inspects you from helm to boot. "Old Meatloaf walks again! Basil sends his thanks, and with them his orders, which are that I am to let you in. Yes, Chef!"

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: He lowers his fork-lance. The gate swings open.
after: He lowers his fork-lance, and the gate swings open.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! Nobody enters Layer-Cake Town until Old Meatloaf has been mended."
after: Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! By my oath, nobody enters Layer-Cake Town until Old Meatloaf has been mended."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "It is Basil's request, so speak to Basil: he is in the Grand Pantry's square, east of the Soup Fountain. Yes, Chef!"
after: "It is Basil's request, so it is Basil you must speak to. You will find him in the Grand Pantry's square, east of the Soup Fountain. Yes, Chef!"

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Sir Loin peers past you toward the Pantry. "Old Meatloaf is up and clanking about? Then the mending is done, and Basil has not sent word."
after: Sir Loin peers past you toward the Pantry. "Old Meatloaf is up and clanking about? Then the mending is done, and yet Basil has not sent me word of it."

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: "Tell Basil yourself: the Grand Pantry's square, east of the Soup Fountain. His word opens this gate, and then the town is yours. Yes, Chef!"
after: "Go and tell Basil yourself, in the Grand Pantry's square, east of the Soup Fountain. His word opens this gate, and then the town is yours. Yes, Chef!"

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! Old Meatloaf is still in two pieces, and I have Basil's list right here."
after: Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! Old Meatloaf is still in two pieces, and I have Basil's list right here, so pray attend."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Colonel Casserole tips his lid. "A fair fight, well fought. The Pancake Plateau is open to you. Mind the syrup; it pools."
after: Colonel Casserole tips his lid. "A fair fight and well fought, and I have not enjoyed one so much in years. The Pancake Plateau is open to you. Do mind the syrup, because it pools."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Colonel Casserole bubbles ominously. "Halt! This gate is guarded by a Colonel."
after: Colonel Casserole bubbles ominously. "Halt, if you please! This gate is guarded by a Colonel, and the Colonel takes his guarding seriously."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "No passes, no bribes - challenge me to single combat with cards. I shall defend this gate to the last course."
after: "I accept no passes and no bribes. You must challenge me to single combat with cards, and I shall defend this gate to the last course."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: "If you win, you pass. If you lose, you do the washing up. Both are honourable."
after: "If you win, you pass, and if you lose, you do the washing up. Both are honourable, and in my time I have done my share of each."

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Professor Pate, Keeper of the Cookbook. I've read every recipe twice; the footnotes have an excellent finish.
after: I am Professor Pate, Keeper of the Cookbook. I have read every recipe in it twice, and the footnotes a third time for pleasure, because the footnotes have an excellent finish.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce, and believe me, I looked. I even licked the index.
after: I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce in any edition, and believe me, I looked everywhere. I am a little ashamed to tell you that I even licked the index.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Four questions about the Gourmands: who they are, what they cook, how their golems speak. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Endless Buffet.
after: I shall ask you four questions about the Gourmands: who they are, what they cook and how their golems speak. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Endless Buffet.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Answer well and earn gold, glory and the respect of a very old book. Answer poorly and earn a gentle, scholarly sigh, lightly salted.
after: Answer well and you earn gold, glory and the respect of a very old book. Answer poorly and you earn only a gentle, scholarly sigh, lightly salted.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.
after: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once, hot and free and properly balanced, and then came the paste, which has no finish at all.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: *brass fanfare* CHEF FLAMBE FONTAINE, LIVE FROM THE CANDY FIELD: DINNER IN A DASH! The Test Kitchen cancelled us, so this is a SECRET BROADCAST!
after: *brass fanfare* It's CHEF FLAMBE FONTAINE, LIVE FROM THE CANDY FIELD, with DINNER IN A DASH! The Test Kitchen cancelled us, my friends, so tonight you are watching a SECRET BROADCAST!

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Seven seasons on the air, and people STILL do my WHOOSH in the street! I'd do it for you now, but I save it for the cameras.
after: Seven seasons on the air, and people STILL do my WHOOSH at me in the street! I would do it for you right now, but a professional saves the whoosh for the cameras.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: My arch-rival, Chef Savannah Souffle, stole my Spaghetti Surprise. The surprise was more spaghetti. She took a job at the Test Kitchen. I wish her well, very far away.
after: My arch-rival, Chef Savannah Souffle, stole my Spaghetti Surprise, and the surprise was more spaghetti. She took a job at the Test Kitchen afterwards, and I wish her well, very far away from here.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Tonight's show: ORDER UP! Six tickets, one counter, no mercy. Stack each dish in the right order before the timer dings. Rewards for performance, and a first-time bonus!
after: Tonight's show is ORDER UP! Six tickets, one counter and no mercy, so stack each dish in the right order before the timer dings. There are rewards for performance, and a first-time bonus!

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: My Turbo Tots toys were recalled for spinning too well, and tonight's audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche. But the show goes on! Let's COOK!
after: My Turbo Tots toys were recalled for spinning too well, and tonight's studio audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche, but the show goes on, as it always has! Let's COOK!

speaker: (minigame host)
before: Back for another shift, champ? Smile for the cameras! They ran out of film years ago, but a professional smiles anyway.
after: Back for another shift, my friend? Then smile for the cameras! They ran out of film years ago, I admit, but a professional smiles anyway.

speaker: (minigame host)
before: Remember, the ticket is your friend. It's judging you, of course, but kindly.
after: And remember, the ticket is your friend. It is also your critic, of course, but unlike a certain chef I could name, it reviews you kindly.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: ORDER UP - THAT COUNTER IS BEAUTIFUL! You cook like someone who knows exactly where the camera is!
after: ORDER UP, and would you LOOK at that counter, it's BEAUTIFUL! You cook like somebody who knows exactly where the camera is!

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Your very first shift on the show! Here's your bonus, free and with no obligation: a scroll!
after: That was your very first shift on the show, so here's your bonus, free and with no obligation whatsoever: a scroll!

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Chef Savannah would call it Scroll Deluxe. She could put a garnish on the envelope and call it a course.
after: Chef Savannah would call it Scroll Deluxe, naturally. That woman could put a garnish on the envelope and call it a course.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Not quite, chef - breathe! Even a souffle gets a second rise in my kitchen!
after: Not quite, chef, but breathe, breathe! Even a souffle gets a second rise in my kitchen, and I have never once said that about Savannah's.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Re-tie your apron and try again! Those tickets can wait; this is a cooking show, not a farewell episode!
after: Re-tie your apron and try again! Those tickets can wait for you, because this is a cooking show and not a farewell episode!

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: The stew thickens. The ladle hums. A small, heavy parcel rises out of the steam: the pot has given you its seasoning.
after: The stew thickens and the ladle begins to hum, and a small, heavy parcel rises out of the steam: the pot has given you its seasoning.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: The stew sits perfectly seasoned. Nothing left to cook.
after: The stew sits perfectly seasoned, and there is nothing left to cook.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: You watch the stew go bland. The pot sighs like a recipe being ignored.
after: You watch the stew go bland, and the pot sighs like a recipe being ignored.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A single sad bubble rises and pops. That was all it had to say.
after: A single sad bubble rises and pops, and that seems to be all the pot has to say about it.

speaker: Basil
before: Over here, quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu at all? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
after: Psst. Over here, and quietly, please. Um, have you ever eaten somewhere that has no menu at all? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.

speaker: Basil
before: There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.
after: There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes, and it says 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it, and I'll tell you where to sit.

speaker: Basil
before: The card's in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. It's golden, so you'll know it when you see it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
after: Um, the card's in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. It's golden, so you'll know it the moment you see it, and Chef always said gold means sit down.

speaker: Basil
before: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited, I think - it feels a lot like being terrified.
after: That's it, that's really it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I think I'm excited, only it feels an awful lot like being terrified, so I can't be sure.

speaker: Basil
before: The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.
after: The sliding door to Omakase is open now, so you just... you leave your fate to the chef, that's how it works in there. (quietly) Yes, Chef.

speaker: (narration)
before: It has been stirring for ten years and nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.
after: It has been stirring for ten years, and in all that time nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.

speaker: (narration)
before: Four dishes are served to the panel. They want to see that you can field real, living units, not just soup.
after: Four dishes are served to the panel, who want to see that you can field real, living units and not just soup.

speaker: (narration)
before: You twist the valve. The cannon coughs, sighs, and settles into a sulk. Your units feel sturdier in a kitchen that is slightly less likely to fire at them.
after: You twist the valve, and the cannon coughs, sighs and settles into a sulk. Your units feel sturdier in a kitchen that is slightly less likely to fire at them.

speaker: (narration)
before: He presses a stained notebook into your hands: habits, weak spots, and a very detailed list of everything the impostor will not eat. The list is everything. Your units hit harder.
after: He presses a stained notebook into your hands: habits, weak spots, and a very detailed list of everything the impostor will not eat, which turns out to be everything. Your units hit harder.

speaker: (narration)
before: The guards pay you without a question. You pocket the coins and feel sick.
after: The guards pay you without a single question, and you pocket the coins and feel sick.
